title: (RHBA-2016:1393) kernel bug fix update
portal_summary:
Updated kernel packages that fix one bug are now available for Red Hat
Enterprise Linux 5.

Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

For details on how to apply this update, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258
portal_description:
The kernel packages contain the Linux kernel, the core of any Linux operating
system.

This update fixes the following bug:

* Previously, when a default Access Control List (ACL) was definied in a
Filesystem in Userspace (FUSE) mountpoint, the ACL was not inherited correctly
by the new file from parent default ACL. Consequently, the new file did not have
the correct permissions, potentially preventing manipulation. With this update,
the underlying source code has been fixed, and thus the default ACL permissions
are no longer inherited as 'r--' permissions. As a result, ACL permissions are
now set correctly and the target user is able to manipulate the file in the
described scenario. (BZ#1326905)

Users of kernel are advised to upgrade to these updated packages, which fix
these bugs. The system must be rebooted for this update to take effect.
